findings.cause: In `projectViewSourceGestures`, `track.flatMap(...)` validates each projected piece with `validateViewGesturePiece(piece, shotStartMs, shotEndMs)`, but it skips gestures completely outside the shot window without validating their source gesture bounds and representation. An invalid source gesture or reachMs/recoverMs specification is thus concealed when projected into an empty slice.
findings.fix: Iterate and validate every source gesture in the track against defaults/representation or call `validateViewGesturePiece(piece, ...)` appropriately before filtering or return empty, ensuring invalid commands throw even when projected into non-intersecting slices.

findings.cause: `registeredBodyView(character)` uses `character.appearance` before `appearance` is assigned (or `character` was created from `appearance` which only holds view/body, but `registeredBodyView` requires `character` or `profile`). More crucially, `registeredBodyView(character).nearHand` is evaluated on `character`, but `nearHand` depends on `character.appearance.bodyView`. In `lila-right`, `layout[0]` is lila with `three-quarter-left` (nearHand='right') and karo with `three-quarter-right` (nearHand='left'). `registeredBodyView(templates[0]!.character)` is used instead of re-deriving for the actual shot primary in `bindActorShot` / runner context, causing `rig` and `profile` to remain static to `templates[0]` instead of matching the primary actor profile/rig in alternating lead shots.
findings.fix: Pass the per-shot derived performer profile and rig when binding or querying, or update `f.profile` / `f.rig` where required by using `shotPerformer` results.

adjudication.reason: The supplied projector calls validateViewSourceGestureTrack before flatMap. Inside each source iteration it checks fractional-event representability before computing the intersection and before if(end<=start)return []. Thus invalid command/overlap/bounds/non-default fractional event is not hidden by an empty slice. Declared source tests cover this, but have NOT RUN.

appearance is initialized from the selected actor/view before ActorDefinitionSchema.parse; registeredBodyView(character).nearHand uses that actor definition, inside templates.map. It is not queried on templates[0]. The base profile/rig seed is Lila, while bindActorShot calls shotPerformer, derives the actual primary actorProfile/buildRig and binds the host identity. Native-head source tests declare both stagings and lead swaps, but have NOT RUN.
